---
title: Time bucket gapfill
description: Use gapfilling to create contiguous time buckets and fill missing data with interpolation or LOCF
products: [cloud, mst, self_hosted]
keywords: [hyperfunctions, Toolkit, gapfilling, interpolate]
---

import * as C from "@constants";

Sometimes data sorted into {C.TIME_BUCKET}s can have gaps. This can happen if you
have irregular sampling intervals, or you have experienced an outage of some
sort. If you have a {C.TIME_BUCKET} that has no data at all, the average returned
from the {C.TIME_BUCKET} is NULL, which could cause problems. You can use a
gapfilling function to create additional rows of data in any gaps, ensuring that
the returned rows are in chronological order, and contiguous. The {C.TIME_BUCKET}
gapfill function creates a contiguous set of {C.TIME_BUCKET}s but does not fill the
rows with data. You can create data for the new rows using another function,
such as last observation carried forward (LOCF), or interpolation.

For more information about gapfilling and interpolation API calls, see the
[hyperfunction API documentation](/reference/timescaledb/hyperfunctions/time_bucket_gapfill/time_bucket_gapfill).
